timing.record_budget: At most 64 emitted records per process. A slot is reserved at construction; an already-started scope retains its slot. Only a successful writer span under 20000000 ns that produced no bytes returns its slot. Printed slots never return.
timing.capture: At most eight static-labelled marks and 64 phase characters. Diagnostic BOOTTIME sampling errors are None and never propagate or affect a safety check. No new live.current(), refresh(), authority validation, I/O recovery or retry is called by the helper.
timing.refresh: The timing guard is declared before the original serial permit. Original started and ended are copied, never replaced. Additional test-only markers identify acceptance and consumer-barrier completion. Drop writes only after the permit and existing refresh-failure latch have dropped.
timing.writer: The outer timing guard outlives the original dispatch call. A nested callback guard only writes timestamps to the fixed local mark array; it performs no stderr I/O. The outer guard prints after dispatch returned or unwound and released its original lease/revocation guard.
timing.labels: read-lease-start/done include the original read_lease lock. read-lease-done to use-verified also includes the original comparison, verify_use lock and its clock validation. use-verified to callback-entry includes original dispatch lock wait plus validation/witness creation, NOT pure mutex-wait time. callback-entry/exit bound original callback work while that lock is held; they are a lower bound for the total lock-hold interval.
timing.outcomes: reported_outcome=None means only scope termination without an explicit outcome declaration; it does not classify a fixture as failed. Only an actual Ok result or the original successful refresh final check sets Some("Ok").
limitations: Missing/suppressed records do not prove absence of work. Sequence numbers include scopes that may be suppressed.
The current helper does not split kernel scheduling, filesystem I/O and CPU inside a measured phase.
Instrumentation overhead can affect timing; a new run remains evidence for its exact new source only.
